title: Fluid Responsiveness Tested by the Effective Pulmonary Blood Flow During a Positive End-expiratory Trial
brief_summary: Fluid responsiveness is difficult to assess at the bedside. The accuracy of published techniques to detect preload-dependent patients have many pitfalls and limitations. The present study test the role of noninvasive effective pulmonary blood flow measured by expired carbon dioxide to detect fluid responsivess in mechanically ventilated patients.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Written informed consent
* Programmed cardiac and noncardiac surgeries
* Need of invasive arterial blood pressure monitoring.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Emergency surgeries.
* Acute pulmonary diseases
* Arrhytmias
* Congestive cardiac failure
study_population: Cardiac and noncardiac surgery patients ASA 2-4
